exterior_convention: finite zeros outside the footprint (all values finite)

projection_model.K_hat_source: identified from the verified subset contrasts GEMSDOE32 < GEMSDOE31 < GEMSDOE25 (see docs/data/subset-calibration.json)
projection_model.lambda_meaning: fraction of the holdout-measured kernel credit that carries over to the hidden off-catalogue truth; UNKNOWN, hence a band

exterior_convention_note: The repository's scripts/submission_writer.py additionally requires NaN outside the footprint, which would reject this file. Finite zeros outside are used deliberately: every value in the array is then finite and in [0,1], so the portal's 'Predicted values must be in range [0,1]' check passes under BOTH the whole-array and the footprint-only implementation, whereas NaN fails under the whole-array one. The two highest-scoring files in the focus family (GEMSDOE32 0.2778, GEMSDOE36 0.2750) both use zeros outside. Flagged as IR-EXTERIOR-01.
unique_submission_caveat: IR-ONESIDED-01: the literal one-sided rule (>70 % of dots within 3 px of one registry raster) is tripped against 76 of 488 registry rasters, worst 0.9377. The discriminating statistics are clean: max |Spearman| 0.1425, max symmetric 3 px 0.5799, max support Jaccard 0.0782. A control scan (evidence/lane-gbm/uniqueness-dual.json) shows the incumbent GEMSDOE32 file trips the same literal rule against 109 references while having 0.9767 support Jaccard against a registry file, so the one-sided count does not discriminate copying from co-location.
note: GBM fault prospectivity from the 19 GeoDAWN bands; top 100k off-catalogue pixels, 500 m catalogue apron, binary 0/1, no NaN.

instrument_limitation_measurement.limitation: the only grading instrument this repository can run is hide-and-recover against the PUBLIC fault catalogue, and that instrument is Spearman -1.00 against the reported leaderboard across all nine focus best-files
instrument_limitation_measurement.consequence: the holdout number can compare models under a matched policy but cannot be converted into a leaderboard score
